---
title: "Amber.jl tutorials"
subtitle: "Build circuits in Julia, then ask them useful questions"
---

Amber is a native Julia circuit simulator. A circuit is ordinary Julia code:
nodes are values, components connect those nodes, and analyses return objects
that can be inspected with Julia.

This is a new, executable-first documentation series. It deliberately begins
with the small concepts that every later example relies on. Read the pages in
order if Amber is new to you:

1. [Your first circuit](tutorials/01-first-circuit.qmd) introduces nodes,
   ground, components, SI units, and structural checks.
2. [Operating point](tutorials/02-operating-point.qmd) solves DC voltages and
   currents.
3. [Transient analysis](tutorials/03-transient.qmd) adds time and waveforms.
4. [Small-signal AC](tutorials/04-small-signal.qmd) computes a frequency
   response around a bias point.
5. [Hierarchy](tutorials/05-hierarchy.qmd) turns repeated circuitry into
   reusable subcircuits.
6. [Diagnostics](tutorials/06-diagnostics.qmd) shows how Amber explains common
   modeling mistakes.

Continue with the AmberMakie notebooks when you are ready to turn those result
objects into engineering views:

7. [Your first AmberMakie plot](tutorials/07-ambermakie-first-plot.qmd) plots
   transient signals and reads exact samples back from a cursor.
8. [Frequency response](tutorials/08-ambermakie-frequency-response.qmd) builds
   linked Bode and Nyquist views.
9. [Spectrum and harmonics](tutorials/09-ambermakie-spectrum.qmd) moves from a
   time-domain waveform to distortion metrics.
10. [Noise analysis](tutorials/10-ambermakie-noise.qmd) visualizes density,
    integrated noise, and component contributions.
11. [Monte Carlo](tutorials/11-ambermakie-monte-carlo.qmd) explores distributions,
    yield, and parameter correlation.

## More ambitious projects

These longer notebooks combine modeling, nonlinear transient simulation,
measurement, and visualization:

12. [Switching buck converter](tutorials/12-buck-converter-project.qmd) models
    an event-driven power stage with switch and diode nonidealities.
13. [CMOS ring oscillator](tutorials/13-cmos-ring-oscillator-project.qmd) builds
    a hierarchical transistor-level oscillator and measures its settled spectrum.
14. [Hodgkin--Huxley neuron](tutorials/14-hodgkin-huxley-project.qmd) uses Amber's
    equation-oriented behavioral sources to solve a biological dynamical system.
15. [CMOS inverter characterization](tutorials/15-cmos-inverter-project.qmd)
    extracts a DC transfer curve and transient propagation delay from the same
    transistor-level cell.

## What you need

Use Julia 1.10 or later. From a clone of Amber, activate the repository and
load the package:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("path/to/Amber.jl")
Pkg.instantiate()

using Amber
```

All examples use Amber's typed SI scales: `1kΩ`, `10nF`, `2ms`, and `1MHz`
are plain numerical values expressed in base SI units. No SPICE suffix rules
are involved.

For the plotting notebooks, activate the `AmberMakie` subproject instead. It
contains AmberMakie, CairoMakie, and the local Amber checkout used by every
executable example.
